transcript.content: Hi, it’s good to meet you. What brings you in today?

Um… yeah, thank you for seeing me. I’m not totally sure how to say it without sounding… off, I guess.

I came in because I’ve been hearing Garrett’s voice. Not like a memory exactly—more like he’s right there, behind me, when I’m out on the trail or in my painting room. It’s very clear. And I know, at least part of me knows, that he’s dead… but in the moment it feels completely real. Does that make sense?
Did hearing Garrett’s voice start after he died?

Yes… after he died, but not right away in that normal grieving way, if that makes sense. I didn’t hear him like that before.

It really started during this stretch where I was kind of… wired. Barely sleeping, taking on way too much, feeling like I had to keep going. I know that probably sounds bad. But it wasn’t just missing him or thinking about him—it started with that shift.
During that wired stretch, did you feel like you needed much less sleep than usual?

Yeah… I did. I mean, I told myself I was just being productive, but for weeks I was sleeping maybe two or three hours a night and still feeling kind of wired, like I didn’t really need more.

And then it shifted. I started sort of crashing, but not in a restful way—broken, heavy sleep, and I’d still wake up exhausted and panicky before dawn. Is that… the kind of thing you mean?
During that wired period, did you feel unusually powerful or specially chosen?

I’m… not sure I’d put it that way. “Powerful” or “chosen” sounds pretty dramatic, and I don’t want to overstate it.

I think I felt more… driven? Like things had unusual importance, maybe, but I don’t know if that counts as specially chosen. I’m sorry—am I answering that clearly enough?
Have you heard Garrett’s voice during times when your mood felt normal—not especially wired or depressed?

No… I don’t think so. At least, not when I felt like myself.

It started during that wired stretch—when I wasn’t really sleeping and I was taking on these impossible things and feeling like I had to keep going. Before that shift, I’d never heard him that way. And it didn’t feel like just… ordinary grief, or missing him. Does that answer what you mean?
During that wired period, did your behavior cause serious problems in your life?

Yeah… I mean, I wanted to believe I was still managing it, but looking back, yes. It caused real problems.

I couldn’t really practice safely. I started cancelling patient sessions, and I got behind on documentation in a way that wasn’t like me. At home it got bad enough that my wife called crisis services because I couldn’t trust myself to be alone.

I guess being admitted to the hospital was the point where I couldn’t really tell myself it was “just stress” anymore. Work, home, safety… it all kind of stopped functioning. Does that answer what you’re asking?
During that wired stretch, did you feel unusually euphoric or intensely upbeat?

At first… yes, I think so. I wouldn’t say I was just “happy,” exactly, but I felt almost lit up. Like there was this urgent purpose to everything I was doing, and I could see it when other people couldn’t.

But if someone questioned me or tried to slow me down, I’d get… much angrier than I want to admit. I’d snap. So it wasn’t only upbeat. It was like this intense drive, and then rage if anything got in the way.

Is that the kind of thing you mean?
After that wired period ended, did you go through a stretch where you felt depressed most of the day nearly every day?

Yes… after that, I did. I tried to tell myself it was just recovery, or exhaustion from everything, but it’s been more than that.

The depressed, shut-down part has been going on for… about four months now, most days. I don’t know if I’m saying that the right way, but yes, it’s been pretty constant.
While you’ve been in this depressed period, have you still been hearing Garrett’s voice?

Not really in the same way, no.

Garrett’s voice started during that wired stretch, when I was barely sleeping and taking on… honestly, impossible things, and I felt like I had to keep going. I hadn’t heard him like that before all of that shifted.

I mean, I’d grieved him before, of course, but this wasn’t just ordinary grief. It felt different. I’m not sure if that’s the distinction you’re asking about.
